the SR is not a prerequisite for contraction in vertebrates, but that it is a crucial factor in the evolution of the mammalian heart.
the evolution of the heart in vertebrates has been accompanied by the development of a highly efficient and specialized SR.
the SR is not essential for the generation of force, but it is required to maintain a constant and high rate of force production in vertebrates.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the SR is an essential component of the vertebrate cardiomyocyte, and that its recruitment is linked to the evolution of the cardiac syncytium.
the SR is a key component of vertebrate cardiomyocyte function, but the extent to which it is used varies with the structural organization of each species.
the SR is a relatively late evolutionary acquisition of the vertebrate cardiomyocyte and is a key component of the transition to a more complex cardiac design and function.

the evolution of the SR is intimately tied to the evolution of the cardiomyocytes in which it resides.
